dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Recently, there's been quite a few outlanders who have come to Ritou specifically to take part in the Irodori Festival. As such, it's up to us here in the International Trade Association to welcome them warmly.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: From the moment we were notified that Ritou would be the festival site, which would be excellent for business, everyone's spirits really picked up.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Whether you may have goods to sell or if you'd just like to know more about the festival events, feel free to ask me.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: So, is there anything I can help with? Do tell.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Oh? Do you require the assistance of the International Trade Association? Please, do tell.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About yourself...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: I'm Kurisu from Fontaine. My real name is actually Christopher, but I've been here so long that it seemed suitable to change it to fit the local customs.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: I'm currently in charge of the International Trade Association. My main task is to be the bridge between everyone here and the Shogunate officials.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: We're all considered outlanders here regardless of where you are from, so we've got to take care of each other.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: It's not an easy life abroad for folks like us. Hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the outlanders in Ritou...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Agh, I hardly even want to talk about it. It's just getting more and more difficult nowadays...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Not only have they limited our trading time and locations, they've also added tax items for various reasons. The biggest headaches are those bureaucrats from the Kanjou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Every now and then, they will come here and pick on us for whatever reason. It's just...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: ...Ah, alas! Anyway, the merchant guild and I have dedicated ourselves to providing every outlander with support.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: You too. Our doors are always open to friendly outlanders.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Oh yes, it has been a while indeed, Traveler. How's everything?

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: You have been doing the International Trade Association a great many favors. I deeply appreciate it. If you need anything, I will try my best to help you out.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: If it is not too much trouble, could you also help send my regards to Miss Kamisato? If you and Miss Kamisato need anything here, feel free to come find me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the outlanders in Ritou...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Since the head of the Hiiragi Clan was removed from his post, all the affairs of the Kanjou Commission have been well-regulated.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Taxes were reduced, and the officials and soldiers made things less difficult for the merchants. Everyone is really relieved.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: However, there is still a lot to be done here. The source of goods, delivery routes and channels... There are still many things to settle.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Anyway, the Trade Association and I have dedicated ourselves to providing every outlander with support.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the outlanders in Ritou...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Since the head of the Hiiragi Clan was removed from his post, all the affairs of the Kanjou Commission have been well-regulated.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Taxes were reduced, and the officials and soldiers made things less difficult for the merchants. Everyone is really relieved, to be honest, and the number of merchants willing to set up shop here in Ritou has increased.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: We've got quite a few new arrivals who aren't yet used to the paths through which goods may be sourced or transported, and so that's where we come in.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Anyway, the Trade Association and I have dedicated ourselves to providing every outlander with the support they need.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Duel

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: I have lost, and must admit that I'm not good enough...

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Haha, maybe it's a businessman's intuition that prevails...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sounds painful.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: Haha. There might be a few tricky problems here and there, but I get a boost of determination seeing everyone's smiling faces after the problem has been resolved.

dialogues.speaker: Kurisu
dialogues.text: We live in an ever-changing world, so we need to be prepared for all kinds of situations. For the sake of the continued prosperity of the International Trade Association, there's still a lot of work that I need to do.
